title: Dimension and inclusion of algebraic tangent cones at a smooth ambient point
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $Y$ be a smooth separated geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $p\in Y(k)$ [def-pc-rational-point]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Then $d=\dim Y$ is a finite nonnegative integer [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and the $k$-vector space $E=T_{Y/k,p}$ has dimension $d$ [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. Let $Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be a reduced closed subscheme containing $p$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme], let $R=\mathcal O_{Z,p}$ be its local ring [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and let $\mathfrak m$ be the maximal ideal of $R$. The algebraic tangent cone
$$C_pZ=\operatorname{Spec}\left(\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}\right)$$
[def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring] is canonically a closed subscheme of the affine space associated to $E$. Here the affine space associated to $E$ has coordinate ring the symmetric algebra on the dual $E^*=\operatorname{Hom}_k(E,k)$, that is, the tensor algebra modulo the relations $v\otimes w-w\otimes v$. One has
$$\dim C_pZ=\dim R\le\dim Z\le d,$$
where ring dimension is [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. If $|Z|\ne|Y|$, then $\dim C_pZ<d$. If $D$ is a smooth locally closed $k$-subscheme of $Y$ containing $p$ with $|D|\subseteq|Z|$, then the differential identifies $T_{D/k,p}$ with a linear subspace of $E$ whose associated affine subspace has underlying space contained in $|C_pZ|$. Locally closed means closed in an open subscheme of $Y$ [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 00KQ (proposition-dimension), Tag 00P6 (lemma-dimension-graded), Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded), Tag 00OU (lemma-dimension-closed-point-finite-type-field). Geometric formulation used in Milne, Abelian Varieties, I.3.6, printed p.18: C_P(V_H) contained in C_P(Z) contained in Tgt_P(V), and dim C_P(Z)=dim Z locally at P. For a quotient local ring the associated-graded map is surjective degree by degree; restricting to an open neighbourhood preserves the local ring.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,p}$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_{Y,p}$, and $V=\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$. A rational section induces inverse structural maps on the residue field and $k$, so $\kappa(p)=k$. The smooth-scheme regularity lemma makes $A$ a Noetherian regular local ring. Its dimension is a finite nonnegative integer. The rational-point stalk dimension lemma gives $\dim A=\dim_pY$, and the irreducible locally algebraic dimension lemma gives $\dim_pY=\dim Y$, because $Y$ is integral and locally of finite type over $k$. Thus $d=\dim Y=\dim A$ is finite. The given point ensures that the rings and spaces here are nonempty.

The regular-local graded cotangent criterion gives $\dim_kV=d$ and the canonical graded isomorphism $\mu_A:\operatorname{Sym}_k(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}A$, sending $v_1\cdots v_q$ to the product of representatives modulo $\mathfrak n^{q+1}$. Rational tangent–cotangent duality identifies $E$ with $V^*$. Explicitly, for a basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of $V$, its dual basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ is a basis of $E$, and evaluation sends $v_i$ to the functional $e_j\mapsto\delta_{ij}$. It therefore canonically identifies $V=E^*$, and $\dim_kE=d$, also when $d=0$. The symmetric algebra in this identification is exactly the tensor-algebra quotient in the statement.

source.place: Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded), canonical multiplication map; varieties.tex Tag 0B2E (lemma-tangent-space-rational-point).

proof.text: The affine quotient description of a closed immersion identifies $R$ with $A/I$ for an ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$, and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak nR$. The affine-open stalk localization theorem identifies chart stalks with prime localizations, and the Spec-map stalk localization theorem identifies the actual stalk map with the map on fractions. The quotient map remains surjective after localization: a fraction in the localized quotient lifts by lifting its numerator and denominator, the latter being outside the maximal ideal. A quotient of a finitely generated affine $k$-algebra is generated by the images of the same generators, so $Z$ is locally of finite type over $k$. Ascending chains of ideals of $R$ lift to ascending chains of ideals of $A$, so $R$ is Noetherian. It is nonzero with residue field $k$. The canonical graded map $G(A\to R)$ sends $[a]_q$ to its image $[\bar a]_q$. It is surjective in every degree, since $\mathfrak m^q$ is the image of $\mathfrak n^q$: lift the finitely many coefficients and factors in a sum of products representing an element of $\mathfrak m^q$. Hence the composite $\operatorname{Sym}_k(E^*)\xrightarrow{\mu_A}\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}A\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R$ is a canonical graded surjection. Its spectrum is the required closed subscheme $C_pZ$ of the affine space of $E$, by the same affine quotient characterization of closed immersions.

source.place: Affine quotient characterization (Morphisms Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion); representative calculation for powers and their quotients.

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R$. The maximal-adic graded-length bridge says that $S$ is standard graded over $k$ and $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\dim_kS_j=\mathrm{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^n)$ for every $n\ge1$. The Hilbert–Samuel growth theorem supplies a nonzero polynomial $Q$ agreeing eventually with this length and satisfying $\deg Q=\dim R$. Apply the standard-graded cumulative-dimension lemma to this very $Q$: $\dim S=\deg Q=\dim R$. The ring-dimension definition identifies $\dim\operatorname{Spec}S=\dim S$, giving $\dim C_pZ=\dim R$. This argument permits a nonreduced associated graded ring and a constant $Q$.

source.place: Tag 00P6 (lemma-dimension-graded), cumulative form, combined with the maximal-ideal Hilbert function in proposition-dimension, Tag 00KQ.

proof.text: Apply the rational-point stalk dimension lemma to $Z$: $\dim R=\dim_pZ\le\dim Z$, since $Z$ itself is one of the open neighbourhoods in the definition of $\dim_pZ$. A chain of irreducible closed subsets of $Z$ is a chain of the same length in $Y$, since $Z$ is closed in $Y$; hence $\dim Z\le d$. If $|Z|\ne|Y|$, append $Y$ to any such chain in $Z$. This strictly increases its length because $Y$ is irreducible and every member is contained in the proper closed subset $Z$. Thus every chain in $Z$ has length at most $d-1$, so $\dim C_pZ\le\dim Z<d$. For $d=0$ this shows that no proper $Z$ containing $p$ can occur.

source.place: Definition 0055 (definition-Krull), chain and neighbourhood definitions; varieties.tex 0A21, closed-point dimension.

proof.text: Now let $D$ satisfy the final hypothesis and put $B=\mathcal O_{D,p}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak b$. Smoothness over $k$ makes $D$ reduced and makes $B$ regular local. Since $|D|\subseteq|Z|$, the reduced-source factorization lemma applied to $D\to Y$ gives a factorization $D\to Z\to Y$. Choose the open neighbourhood of $p$ in which $D$ is closed. The affine-open and Spec-map stalk localization theorems identify its local map with the localized coordinate quotient, as in step 3, giving a surjection $A\twoheadrightarrow B$; the stalk is unchanged on that neighbourhood. Factoring through $R$ gives $A\twoheadrightarrow R\twoheadrightarrow B$. Both quotient maps send the maximal ideal onto the maximal ideal, and the residue fields are $k$, since these are the same rational point.

Apply the canonical graded-map construction to $A\twoheadrightarrow R\twoheadrightarrow B$. The maps compose on representatives, and the second is degreewise surjective by the power-lifting argument of step 3. By regularity, $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak b}B=\operatorname{Sym}_k(\mathfrak b/\mathfrak b^2)$ canonically. The degree-one map $V\twoheadrightarrow\mathfrak b/\mathfrak b^2$ is surjective, so its dual is injective: a functional whose pullback vanishes vanishes on every lifted vector. Tangent–cotangent naturality identifies that dual with $\mathrm d(D\to Y)_p$, realizing $T_{D/k,p}$ as a linear subspace of $E$. Under the regular graded identifications, the composite $\operatorname{Sym}_k(E^*)\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak b}B$ is exactly the symmetric-algebra map of this cotangent surjection: on a degree-one class it sends a representative in $A$ to its image in $B$, and agreement on generators determines an algebra map. Consequently its spectrum is the associated affine linear subspace of $E$. It factors through $\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R)=C_pZ$, proving the asserted inclusion of underlying spaces (in fact a closed immersion).
